title: A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture: a finitely generated residually finite group G with cohomological dimension 2 and geometric dimension 3. G is the kernel of the height homomorphism of the right-angled Artin group of a flag triangulation L of the acyclic presentation complex of <x, y | x^2 = y^5, x^2 = (xy^-1)^3>, whose fundamental group has a nontrivial homomorphism into the unit quaternions. The first lesson defines cohomological and geometric dimension and states the theorem. The second proves a localized degree theorem for word maps on unit quaternions. The third turns a two-dimensional classifying space into a presentation whose relators contain prescribed boundary chains. The fourth proves exact signed counts and a uniform quadratic estimate for products of quaternion labels. The fifth solves finite systems of word equations on finite quotients by degree and passes to the group by compactness: if a two-dimensional classifying space existed, small labellings with product 1 around a cycle basis would have product 1 around every closed path. The sixth proves residual finiteness of right-angled Artin groups; the seventh the contractibility of the cube complex of the Artin group, by an algebraic induction over a splitting; the eighth the acyclicity of the zero level, with explicit generators and triangle words. The ninth constructs the acyclic flag complex L and its quaternion representation; the tenth proves the normal form of reduced traces and a slowly varying direction map; the eleventh pulls back flat transport along a slowly varying map to small labellings with nontrivial holonomy, and completes the proof.
prerequisites: core course Algebraic Topology (Fomberg's notes): homotopy invariance of singular homology (Theorem 1.13, Corollary 1.14)
core course Point-Set Topology: the Lebesgue number lemma for compact metric spaces

programme lesson Regular values and degree modulo two (course borsuks-conjecture-in-dimension-nine), Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, Proposition 3.1: Sard's theorem and regular level sets

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg-Ganea conjecture' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026; main.tex with sections introduction, degree, presentation, geometry, transport, conclusion and references.bib; local clone openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 14 and 15 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written: the localized degree by a cyclic group of conjugations; the aligned presentation by three shears; exact counts and the uniform quadratic estimate with its constants; the moving open sets and the degree of the selected word map; finite-coordinate compactness; residual finiteness of graph groups by the semidirect splitting; the cubical universal cover; ascending links, the filtration by heights, the retraction of the half spaces and Mayer-Vietoris; the seed presentation, its quaternion representation and its flag triangulation; reduced traces, local confluence and the direction map; the slowly varying map of the level graph, commuting-power paths and the developing map. No error found. Changes of form in the course: the acyclicity of the universal cover of the torus complex is proved algebraically, by a short exact sequence of the cube complexes of chains over the splitting and the tree of the free group, in place of the tree of spaces and Mayer-Vietoris over finite subtrees; the generators of the level complex are written explicitly as letters s_qr with values a_q^-1 a_r and the triangle words as s_qr s_rs s_qs^-1 and s_rs s_qr s_qs^-1; the numbering of the lemmas follows the lessons. Later literature, read on 15 Oct 2026 in arXiv searches for preprints after the release (queries on Eilenberg-Ganea, Bestvina-Brady, geometric and cohomological dimension, and all abstracts mentioning OpenAI): no other preprint on the Eilenberg-Ganea problem was found; Flores Martinez arXiv:2610.19203 (Euler characteristics of Bestvina-Brady kernels of Artin groups of spherical type) is cited in the eighth lesson. Free sources read: Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups, first edition on the author's page (Sections 8.5, 11.6 and Appendix F.3); Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, free edition (Example 2.38 and the statements cited); Dicks-Leary arXiv:1210.6585 (Theorem 1, Proposition 2 and the remark after Corollary 3); Green's thesis, White Rose eTheses (Corollary 5.4, residual finiteness of graph products, and the Normal Form Theorem 3.9); Cartier-Foata, electronic reedition on D. Foata's page (Chapter I, Section 2, and Krattenthaler's appendix, Definition 2.2 and the section titles); Hsu-Wise, author's version on the McGill page (Theorem 3.7, a short proof of Green's theorem); Gerstenhaber-Rothaus, page scans on PubMed Central (Theorem 1: the degree of the word map of a compact connected Lie group of rank m is d^m). Check program plan/checks_20261015/eg_check.py, run eg_check_run_20261015a.txt (15 Oct 2026): 32 of 32 checks pass. Quaternion estimates on 2000 random cases and the asymptotic sharpness of the commutator estimate; the constants delta = 1/(4C), eta = 1/(16C^2); the three shears P, Q, P of the aligned presentation on 50 random invertible matrices (exact rationals); reduced traces in four right-angled Artin groups (path, triangle with a pendant edge, 4-cycle, two points): uniqueness of the reduced trace under random deletion orders (300 words each), |gx| = |g| +- 1, the bound ||b(gx)-b(g)||_1 <= 2/(n+1) (attained) and the common simplex (400 cases each); the direction vectors of commuting powers; the steps of level edges translated by d^-1 (300 cases); the permutation construction for free groups (500 reduced words); the triangle words have value 1; the seed representation (x^2 = y^5 = -1, Re(xy^-1) = 1/2, (xy^-1)^3 = -1); and the flag complex L of the ninth lesson built explicitly: 103 vertices, 372 edges, 270 triangles, flag, Euler characteristic 1, integral homology of a point by Smith normal forms.

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course, each with its exact statement and free locators in the lesson where it is stated: (CW) covering spaces and cellular chains of a classifying space (first lesson, Section 2; Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 1.3, Propositions 1.33, 1.34, 1.39, 4.1, Lemma 2.34, Theorem 2.35); (DEG) degree on isolating open sets: regular count, excision, homotopy invariance (second lesson, Section 3; Hatcher, Lemma 3.27 and Proposition 2.30); (HE) homotopy equivalences of CW complexes: collapsing a contractible subcomplex, attaching along homotopic maps, cellular approximation of loops, lifting to universal covers, fundamental groups of presentation complexes (third lesson, Section 3; Hatcher, Propositions 0.16, 0.17, 0.18, 1.26, 1A.2, Theorem 4.8); (CUBE) cellular homology of cube complexes with the cubical boundary formula, cells of dimension at least three do not change the fundamental group, and quotients of universal covers by subgroups (seventh lesson; Hatcher, Theorem 2.35, Section 2.2, Propositions 1.26, 1.36, 1.40); (SIMP) simplicial homology equals singular homology, homology of increasing unions, barycentric subdivision, and the Mayer-Vietoris sequence for complexes of convex polytopes (eighth lesson; Hatcher, Theorem 2.27, Proposition 3.33, Sections 2.1 and 2.2); (BARY) the order complex of a regular two-dimensional cell complex is a simplicial complex homeomorphic to it (ninth lesson; Hatcher, Section 2.1); (SC) the three-sphere is simply connected, and covering maps of the universal cover of a simplicial complex (eleventh lesson; Hatcher, Proposition 1.14 and Section 1.3); and (PI1), (COV), (CELL), stated and not proved in the lesson Cone pictures and asphericity of the course on the torsion-free group algebra with zero divisors. A foundation course proving them is requested from the programme coordinator.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
